title: Partir, laisser, peiner et rappeler
summary: Choose the right construction for leaving, having trouble, almost doing something and reminding someone.
objectives: Use `avoir du mal à/avec` and `faillir` + infinitive.
Build a reminder with `rappeler` something to someone or `rappeler à` someone `de` do something.

sources.label: B1 public topic index (coverage reference only)

sections.title: Leaving a place, leaving an object and going out
paragraphs: `Partir` means depart: `partir de Lyon`, `partir pour Lille`. It does not normally take the place left as a direct object. `Quitter` takes a direct object and means leave a place, a job or a person: `quitter le bureau`. `Laisser` takes what or whom you leave behind or in a state: `laisser les clés ici`. `Sortir` means go out of a place, `sortir du bâtiment`; with a direct object it can mean take something out, `sortir les chaises`.

Present paradigms: `partir` gives `je pars, tu pars, il/elle/on part, nous partons, vous partez, ils/elles partent`; `sortir` gives `je sors, tu sors, il/elle/on sort, nous sortons, vous sortez, ils/elles sortent`. `Quitter` gives `je quitte, tu quittes, il/elle/on quitte, nous quittons, vous quittez, ils/elles quittent`. `Laisser` gives `je laisse, tu laisses, il/elle/on laisse, nous laissons, vous laissez, ils/elles laissent`.

In the `passé composé`, `partir` uses `être + parti` with subject agreement; `quitter` and `laisser` use `avoir + quitté/laissé`. `Sortir` uses `être` for going out, but `avoir` when taking a direct object out: `elle est sortie`; `elle a sorti la poubelle`. Vocabulary: `une clé` (feminine), a key; `une poubelle` (feminine), a bin.
points: `Partir` does not always mean leave permanently; `quitter` can also describe leaving a room briefly.
The choice is guided by construction and meaning, not just by the English verb leave.

examples.english: We are leaving Tours tomorrow morning.

examples.french: Elle **quitte** le bureau à dix-huit heures.
examples.english: She leaves the office at six p.m.

examples.french: Je **laisse** les clés chez le voisin.
examples.english: I am leaving the keys at the neighbour's.

examples.french: Il **est sorti** du local après avoir **sorti** les cartons.
examples.english: He left the premises after taking the boxes out.
examples.note: Going out uses `être`; taking something out uses `avoir`.

mistakes.avoid: Je pars le bureau à midi.
mistakes.prefer: Je quitte le bureau à midi.
mistakes.why: `Partir` does not take this place as a direct object; alternatively say `je pars du bureau`.

sections.title: A difficulty with an action or a thing
paragraphs: `Avoir du mal à` + infinitive means have trouble doing something. `Avoir du mal avec` + noun means struggle with something or someone. Conjugate `avoir` for the person and time: `j'ai, tu as, il/elle/on a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont du mal`. `Du mal` remains the same phrase.

This expression describes difficulty, not physical pain. `J'ai mal au dos` means my back hurts; `j'ai du mal à me lever` means I have difficulty getting up. Do not remove `du` or substitute the pain construction when you mean struggle.
points: Vocabulary: `un logiciel` (masculine), a software program; `une prononciation` (feminine), a pronunciation.

examples.french: J'**ai du mal à** comprendre cette annonce.
examples.english: I have trouble understanding this announcement.
examples.note: `À` links the expression to an infinitive.

examples.french: Vous **avez du mal avec** ce logiciel?
examples.english: Are you struggling with this software?

mistakes.why: The action construction requires `à` plus an infinitive.

sections.title: `Faillir` + infinitive: an event nearly happened
paragraphs: `Faillir` + infinitive is especially common in the `passé composé` to say almost did something: `j'ai failli oublier`, I almost forgot. The second verb remains an infinitive and takes no linking `à` or `de`. In the ordinary reading, the near event did not actually happen.

Use `j'ai failli, tu as failli, il/elle/on a failli, nous avons failli, vous avez failli, ils/elles ont failli`. Other uses of `faillir` can mean fail in a duty, but that is a different construction. This lesson trains the common near-event use, not rare present paradigms.
points: `Presque` can express other kinds of almost, including states and amounts; `faillir` is not a replacement for every `presque`.

examples.note: The stop was not missed in the intended reading.

examples.french: Elle **a failli envoyer** le mauvais document.
examples.english: She almost sent the wrong document.

sections.title: Remind someone: the person is introduced by `à`
paragraphs: `Rappeler quelque chose à quelqu'un` means remind someone of something: `rappeler la date à Léa`. Replace the recipient with `lui/leur`: `je lui rappelle la date`. `Rappeler à quelqu'un de` + infinitive means remind someone to do something: `rappelle-moi de réserver`.

`Rappeler` also means call back: `je te rappelle demain`. `Se rappeler` means remember, usually with a direct object: `je me rappelle cette visite`. These meanings are distinguished by their construction and context, not the spelling of the verb alone.

Present forms are `je rappelle, tu rappelles, il/elle/on rappelle, nous rappelons, vous rappelez, ils/elles rappellent`. The future is `rappeller-` plus all six endings, as taught earlier; the past participle is `rappelé`. Vocabulary: `une date` (feminine), a date; `un rendez-vous` (masculine), an appointment.
points: For an idea that reminds you of something, use `rappeler` with a recipient too: `Cette odeur me rappelle la mer`.

examples.french: Je **rappelle la date à** nos partenaires.
examples.english: I remind our partners of the date.
examples.note: The date is the direct object; partners are introduced by `à`.

examples.english: Remind him or her to take their badge.
examples.note: `Lui` is the recipient and `de` introduces the action.

examples.french: Cette chanson **me rappelle** mon premier voyage.
examples.english: This song reminds me of my first journey.
examples.note: The remembered event is a direct object in French.

sections.title: Faillir faire ou faillir ne pas faire
paragraphs: `Faillir` can place either a positive or a negative event just short of happening. `Elle a failli obtenir le remboursement` normally means she nearly got it but did not. `Elle a failli ne pas obtenir le remboursement` normally means she nearly failed to get it but did get it. In the second sentence, `ne pas` denies `obtenir` inside the infinitive group; it does not negate the auxiliary `a`.

A direct-object pronoun belonging to the second verb goes before that infinitive: `avoir failli le supprimer`. It does not move before `avoir` just because the whole sentence is in the `passé composé`. To reconstruct the meaning, first read the infinitive group by itself, including any negation, then apply almost to that event.
points: Vocabulary: `un remboursement` (masculine), a refund. The outcomes described here are the ordinary near-miss readings; the wider story can provide further detail.

examples.french: Elle **a failli obtenir** le remboursement, mais sa demande a finalement été refusée.
examples.english: She almost obtained the refund, but her request was ultimately refused.

examples.french: Elle **a failli ne pas obtenir** le remboursement, mais la décision a été corrigée à temps.
examples.english: She almost failed to obtain the refund, but the decision was corrected in time.
examples.note: The negative event nearly happened instead.

examples.french: Ce fichier, nous **avons failli le supprimer**.
examples.note: `Le` is the object of `supprimer` and stays beside that infinitive.

sections.title: Ce qui rappelle, la personne et le souvenir
paragraphs: In a resemblance or memory sentence, separate three roles: the trigger as subject, the person reminded as indirect object, and the remembered person or thing as direct object. In `Ce geste me rappelle ma sœur`, the gesture triggers the memory, `me` is the person experiencing it, and `ma sœur` is what comes to mind. French does not add an English-style of before that direct object.

A visible `de` is not always a preposition required by `rappeler`. In `Cette photo me rappelle de belles vacances`, `de` is the reduced indefinite article before `belles vacances`, not a link equivalent to English of. Replacing that whole remembered noun phrase with `celles de mon enfance` removes that article: `Cette photo me rappelle celles de mon enfance`.
points: Vocabulary: `un geste` (masculine), a gesture; `une sœur` (feminine), a sister; `les vacances` (feminine plural), holidays.

examples.english: That gesture reminds me of my sister.
examples.note: No `de` is placed before the person remembered.

examples.french: Cette photo **me rappelle de belles vacances**.
examples.english: This photo reminds me of lovely holidays.
examples.note: `De` belongs to the indefinite noun phrase, following the pre-adjective article pattern.

examples.french: Cette photo **me rappelle celles de mon enfance**.
examples.english: This photo reminds me of the holidays of my childhood.
examples.note: `Celles` refers back to `vacances`. The first `de` disappears because it was the noun phrase's article, not `rappeler`'s preposition.

mistakes.avoid: Sa voix me rappelle de mon voisin.
mistakes.prefer: Sa voix me rappelle mon voisin.
mistakes.why: The person remembered is the direct object of `rappeler`; `me` identifies the person reminded.

practice.prompt: Choose the verb that can directly take le bâtiment to mean leave it.
practice.explanation: Quitter takes the place as a direct object; partir would require de.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition: Elle a du mal ___ entendre.
practice.explanation: Use à before the infinitive.

practice.prompt: Supply faillir in the passé composé: Nous ___ oublier les billets.
practice.explanation: Avoir plus failli precedes the infinitive.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition for the person: Je rappelle l'heure ___ Nora.
practice.explanation: Rappeler something à someone.

practice.prompt: Supply partir in the present: Nous ___ pour Brest.
practice.explanation: Nous partons; pour introduces the destination.

practice.prompt: Supply laisser in the present: Je ___ mon sac ici pendant la visite.
practice.explanation: Laisser identifies the object left behind.

practice.prompt: Supply sortir in the passé composé: Elle ___ les chaises sur la terrasse.
practice.explanation: Taking a direct object out requires avoir.

practice.prompt: Supply sortir in the passé composé for going out: Les visiteuses ___ par cette porte.
practice.explanation: Going out takes être and feminine plural agreement.

practice.prompt: Supply the complete phrase meaning have trouble, using avoir in the present: Nous ___ avec cette imprimante.
practice.explanation: Avoir du mal avec introduces the problem noun.

practice.prompt: Complete with the appropriate form of tomber: Elle a failli ___ dans l'escalier.
practice.explanation: Faillir is followed directly by an infinitive.

practice.prompt: Replace à Paul with the recipient pronoun: Je ___ rappelle la réunion.
practice.explanation: The reminder's recipient is indirect, so use lui.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition: Rappelle-moi ___ fermer la fenêtre.
practice.explanation: A reminder to do something uses de + infinitive.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition after partir: Je pars ___ bureau à dix-huit heures. Use de + le.
practice.explanation: Partir uses de for the point of departure.

practice.prompt: Supply à or avec: Tu as du mal ___ ce nouveau clavier.
practice.explanation: Avec introduces the object causing difficulty.

practice.prompt: Choose the ordinary implication of J'ai failli rater le train.
practice.explanation: Faillir + infinitive presents a near event that did not happen.

practice.prompt: Supply rappeler in the present: Vous ___ la date aux participants.
practice.explanation: Present vous uses one l in rappelez, unlike future rappellerez.

practice.prompt: Read J'ai failli ne pas recevoir le colis, mais le gardien l'a récupéré pour moi. What is the ordinary outcome?
choices: I received the parcel despite a near failure.
I definitely did not receive the parcel.
answers: I received the parcel despite a near failure.
practice.explanation: Almost applies to ne pas recevoir; failure to receive nearly happened but was avoided.

practice.prompt: Replace only cette adresse with la: Tu as failli oublier cette adresse. Keep the tense and word order required by the pronoun.
practice.explanation: The object pronoun belongs to oublier and elides before that infinitive; it does not precede as.

practice.prompt: Place ne and pas before the infinitive to mean almost did not find: Nous avons failli ___ trouver la sortie. Give the missing two words.
practice.explanation: Negating the infinitive changes which event was narrowly avoided.

practice.prompt: Remove the one unnecessary word: Ce parfum lui rappelle de sa grand-mère. Write the corrected sentence without changing any other words.
answers: Ce parfum lui rappelle sa grand-mère.
practice.explanation: Lui is the person reminded; sa grand-mère is a direct object and does not take de.

practice.prompt: In Cette mélodie nous rappelle de longues soirées, why is de present?
choices: It is the indefinite article before a plural adjective and noun.
Rappeler always requires de before the remembered thing.
answers: It is the indefinite article before a plural adjective and noun.
practice.explanation: De longues soirées is the direct-object noun phrase; de is its article, not a required preposition of rappeler.

production_task.prompt: Write a message before leaving work. Say when you are leaving, what you are leaving behind, something you nearly forgot, a task you struggle with and a reminder for a colleague.
production_task.model_answer: Je quitte le bureau à dix-sept heures. Je laisse les clés à l'accueil. J'ai failli oublier le dossier, mais il est maintenant dans mon sac. J'ai du mal à utiliser la nouvelle imprimante. Rappelle-moi de demander une démonstration demain.
production_task.translation: I am leaving the office at five p.m. I am leaving the keys at reception. I almost forgot the file, but it is now in my bag. I have trouble using the new printer. Remind me to ask for a demonstration tomorrow.
rubric: Choose the leaving verb according to its object.
Use `à` for the difficult action and `de` for the reminded action.
